name: API Authentication & Security Contract Design
description: Designing API-level authentication schemes, security contract documentation, and abuse prevention architectures at the platform level. CRITICAL CROSS-ROLE DISTINCTION: This skill is fundamentally different from four other roles' security-related skills. Backend's be_auth_security covers implementing bcrypt password hashing, writing JWT signing code, building OAuth2 middleware, and coding RBAC guards (implementation — 'how do I securely code this auth flow?'). Cyber Security's cs_threats_and_attacks covers analyzing attack vectors, conducting penetration testing, and developing exploit payloads (offensive — 'how do I break into this system?'). QA's qa_non_functional_testing.app_security_verification_owasp covers verifying OWASP Top 10 defenses pass quality gates (verification — 'does the security implementation actually work?'). API Design's api_auth_security covers deciding WHICH authentication scheme (API Key, OAuth2, mTLS) belongs in the API contract, how security schemes are documented in OpenAPI securitySchemes, modeling OAuth2 scopes and permission hierarchies at the specification level, and designing organization-wide API abuse prevention policies (strategic contract-level decision-making — 'which auth method should this API's contract specify, and how is it documented for consumers?').

subskills.name: Authentication Scheme Selection & Trade-offs
subskills.description: Evaluating and selecting API authentication schemes for different use-cases — API Key vs OAuth2 vs mTLS vs HMAC signature vs JWT Bearer token trade-off analysis, consumer type mapping (internal service, third-party app, public client), and documenting selection rationale.

subskills.name: OAuth2 API Contract Patterns
subskills.description: Designing OAuth2 integration patterns at the API contract level — specifying grant types per API category (Authorization Code for user-facing, Client Credentials for service-to-service), token endpoint documentation, refresh token policies, and PKCE requirements in OpenAPI securitySchemes.

subskills.name: API Key Lifecycle & Management Policies
subskills.description: Designing API key lifecycle policies — key generation standards, rotation schedules, scoping and rate-limit tiers per key, revocation procedures, key transmission standards (header vs query parameter), and developer portal key provisioning flows.

subskills.name: OAuth2 Scope & Permission Modeling
subskills.description: Designing hierarchical OAuth2 scope taxonomies — scope naming conventions (resource:action format), scope inheritance and composition rules, minimum-privilege scope assignment policies, and consent screen design for third-party API consumers.

subskills.name: Token Exchange & Delegation Patterns
subskills.description: Designing token exchange and delegation flows for complex API ecosystems — RFC 8693 Token Exchange, on-behalf-of (OBO) delegation, token downscoping for microservice chains, and audience-restricted token policies.

subskills.name: API-Specific Threat Modeling
subskills.description: Conducting threat modeling specifically for API surfaces — STRIDE analysis for API endpoints, OWASP API Security Top 10 (Broken Object Level Authorization, Mass Assignment, SSRF), API attack surface mapping, and security requirements documentation per endpoint.

subskills.name: Security Scheme Documentation Standards
subskills.description: Standardizing how security requirements are documented in API specifications — OpenAPI securitySchemes and security requirements objects, authentication flow diagrams in developer portals, error response standards for 401/403, and security onboarding guides for API consumers.

subskills.name: Zero Trust API Architecture Patterns
subskills.description: Designing Zero Trust principles for API platforms — per-request authentication and authorization verification, service identity propagation across API boundaries, certificate-based API identity, and eliminating implicit trust in internal API networks.

subskills.name: API Abuse Prevention Architecture
subskills.description: Designing platform-level API abuse prevention systems — bot detection strategies, credential stuffing defense at API gateway level, anomalous usage pattern detection, progressive security challenges (CAPTCHA escalation), and API fraud scoring architectures.
